review_notes: Read the whole target file and the sibling files it copies: Pair/EnergyReturn.lean (physicalScaling_normSq_le, pair_energy_return, pair_window_return) and Asymptotics/TruncatedScaling.lean (truncatedModeFactor, truncatedModeFactor_pos). Also checked the definitions of exteriorScaling, physicalScaling, exteriorScaling_coordinate, occupationNormSq, and both intertwining theorems. The two proof pairs are the same argument except for the scaling and intertwining lemma used. pair_window_return and truncated_pair_window_return differ only in the omega side goals, so I did not report them. I did not check the exact form of pairFactor_one_le. Both proofs derive 1 ≤ pairFactor^2 from it with nlinarith, so the helper below takes 1 ≤ r as a hypothesis. I could not compile any of the proposed changes.

findings.problem: The proof repeats the body of physicalScaling_normSq_le in Pair/EnergyReturn.lean almost line for line. Both unfold occupationNormSq, apply Finset.sum_le_sum, rewrite with exteriorScaling_coordinate, norm_mul and mul_pow, and bound ‖∏ d i‖ ≤ 1 via norm_prod and Finset.prod_le_one₀. Both then square that bound and finish with mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right ... trans_eq (one_mul _). The only difference is the per-mode fact ‖d i‖ ≤ 1. The general fact is that an exterior scaling with every |d i| ≤ 1 does not increase occupationNormSq, and it is proved twice.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one lemma in EnergyReturn.lean, or in Exterior/OccupationMetric.lean next to exteriorScaling_coordinate:

theorem exteriorScaling_normSq_le (Q : ℕ) (d : Fin (Q+1) → ℂ) (hd : ∀ i, ‖d i‖ ≤ 1) (x : Space Q) :
    occupationNormSq Q (exteriorScaling Q d x) ≤ occupationNormSq Q x

Proof sketch: this is the current block with d in place of the mode factors. Use sum_le_sum, exteriorScaling_coordinate, norm_mul and mul_pow. Then use norm_prod and Finset.prod_le_one₀ with hd to get ‖∏ i ∈ A, d i‖ ≤ 1, square it, and conclude as before.

Then physicalScaling_normSq_le becomes `unfold physicalScaling; exact exteriorScaling_normSq_le Q _ (fun i => by simpa only [Complex.norm_real, Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_nonneg (modeFactor_nonneg Q i.val)] using modeFactor_le_one Q i.val hQ) x`.

truncatedScaling_normSq_le becomes `unfold truncatedScaling; exact exteriorScaling_normSq_le L Q ...`. Its per-mode obligation is the existing residual: `rw [Complex.norm_real, Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_pos (truncatedModeFactor_pos L Q hQ i)]; unfold truncatedModeFactor; split_ifs; exact modeFactor_le_one Q i.val hQ; exact le_rfl`. Pass Q, not L, as the first argument of the helper.
findings.benefit: The product-norm and sum-comparison argument is stated and maintained once. Each scaling lemma then reduces to the one fact that differs, a per-mode bound ‖d i‖ ≤ 1. A change to the occupation metric or to exteriorScaling_coordinate would need one edit, not two copied proofs.

findings.problem: The proof of truncated_pair_energy_return is a copy of pair_energy_return in Pair/EnergyReturn.lean. Only the scaling (physicalScaling or truncatedScaling) and the intertwining lemma differ. Both proofs take occupationNormSq of the intertwining identity S(E x) = r • E'(S x). They rewrite with occupationNormSq_smul, Complex.norm_real and abs_of_nonneg, derive 1 ≤ r^2 by nlinarith, and run the same three-step calc: u ≤ r^2·u = ‖S(E x)‖² ≤ ‖E x‖². The argument that a scalar r ≥ 1 intertwining with a norm-nonincreasing S gives a return bound is real reasoning, and it is written twice.
findings.proposed_change:
Add an abstract lemma next to occupationNormSq_smul in EnergyReturn.lean:

theorem occupationNormSq_le_of_smul_eq (Q : ℕ) (r : ℝ) (hr : 1 ≤ r) (u v w : Space Q)
    (h : w = (r : ℂ) • u) (hw : occupationNormSq Q w ≤ occupationNormSq Q v) :
    occupationNormSq Q u ≤ occupationNormSq Q v

Proof sketch: subst h and rw [occupationNormSq_smul, Complex.norm_real, Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_nonneg (by linarith)] at hw. Then 1 ≤ r^2 by nlinarith, and u ≤ r^2·u by mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right with occupationNormSq_nonneg.

Then pair_energy_return becomes `exact occupationNormSq_le_of_smul_eq Q _ (pairFactor_one_le Q p hp) _ _ _ (sourcePair_intertwining Q p hQ hp x) (physicalScaling_normSq_le Q hQ _)`.

truncated_pair_energy_return becomes `exact occupationNormSq_le_of_smul_eq Q _ (pairFactor_one_le Q p hp) _ _ _ (truncated_sourcePair_intertwining L Q p hQ hp hL x) (truncatedScaling_normSq_le L Q hQ _)`. This assumes pairFactor_one_le states 1 ≤ pairFactor Q p, which its use here suggests. If it states something else, adjust hr accordingly.
findings.benefit: Each theorem shrinks from about 15 lines to one application, and its two inputs (the intertwining identity and the norm bound) are visible. The scalar/norm manipulation, which is easy to get subtly wrong, lives in one place instead of drifting between a physical and a truncated copy.
